15	- Use the theme package's constants (ColorPrimary, ColorError, etc.)
16	- A text colour reaches 4.5:1 (`theme.ContrastRatio`) on the surface it is painted on, on each shipped theme: `ColorText`, `ColorDim`, `ColorSubTitleFg`, `ColorWarn`, `ColorFooterWarn`, `ColorFooterError` (`TestEveryTextColourReachesItsContrastOnEveryTheme`, DEVDESK-764), and, from DEVDESK-770, `ColorSecondary` (4.5:1 on the background, 3:1 on the selected row), `ColorTableHeaderFg`, `ColorPrimary`, `ColorTitleFg`, `ColorAppTitleFg`, `ColorSeverityHigh` and `ColorSeverityLow` (4.5:1 on the background, 3:1 on the selected row; the badge text is `ColorBackground`, D181), plus the pairs of the active tab, the focused primary button, the unfocused primary and secondary buttons and the inactive command line (`TestEveryTextPairReachesItsContrastOnEveryTheme`) and the four severity badges (`TestEverySeverityBadgeReachesTextContrastOnEveryTheme`); the frame border `ColorViewportBorder` reaches 3:1 on the background (a non-text object, WCAG 1.4.11, D179), and it is also the gauge rail (D181), faint under the cursor. What tells "greyed" or "secondary" apart is not always the shade, and the code holds exactly this: the disabled button is italic (`TestTheDisabledButtonDiffersFromAnEnabledOneByMoreThanColour`); a greyed shortcut keeps its key without bold or a vivid colour; secondary text (`DimStyle`) gets its hierarchy from position and weight, not from italics. On solarized-dark, solarized-light and catppuccin-latte `ColorDim` and `ColorText` are nearly the same tone (delta E 5.6, 0.8 and 4.6), a known limit measured in `docs/measurements/2026-11-24-theme-text-contrast.md` (Rule 130)
17	
18	### Rule 105 : Help message format
19	
20	- Standard format: `[key] action  [key] action`
21	- Displayed with `theme.HelpStyle` (italic + ColorDim)
22	- Keys in square brackets `[]`
23	- Separated by at least 2 spaces
24	
25	### Rule 115 : Uniform background handling (lipgloss)
26	
27	With `app.theme: auto` the OSC 11 query comes before the theme's background: `View().BackgroundColor` stays `nil` while the detection is pending, so the terminal answers with its own color.
28	
29	**lipgloss does NOT propagate a parent's background to its children.**
30	
31	`JoinHorizontal`/`JoinVertical` insert "bare" spaces that show the terminal's native background.
32	
33	| Forbidden | Alternative |
34	|----------|-------------|
35	| `lipgloss.JoinHorizontal` to assemble blocks | Build each line manually with `PadWithBg()` |
36	| `lipgloss.JoinVertical` to stack lines | `strings.Join(lines, "\n")` with each line padded |
37	| `strings.Repeat("\n", n)` for blank lines | `theme.EmptyLineBg(width)` |
38	| `lipgloss.NewStyle().Render(text)` with no background | `.Background(ColorBackground)` mandatory |
39	| Hardcoded hex color | Global variables (`ColorBackground`, `ColorDim`, etc.) |
40	
41	`JoinHorizontal`/`JoinVertical` are acceptable **only** if the result is wrapped in a `.Background(ColorBackground).Width(w)` style.
42	
43	`lipgloss.Place` → always use `WithWhitespaceStyle(lipgloss.NewStyle().Background(theme.ColorBackground))`
44	(Lip Gloss v2 removed `WithWhitespaceBackground`).
45	
46	**Safety net, not a replacement (DEVDESK-209).** The router asks the terminal to
47	use `ColorBackground` as its default background (`tea.View.BackgroundColor`). The
48	helpers above stay mandatory: the native background is absent in 16-colour
49	terminals, under `NO_COLOR`, without a TTY, in a terminal or tmux that ignores
50	OSC 11, and during a `tea.ExecProcess` (the child sees the terminal's own
51	default). A bare cell there shows the user's background. See
52	`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.
53	
54	**Known gap: the text input's cursor cell.** In Bubbles v2 the virtual cursor
55	(`textinput.Styles.Cursor`) carries a colour and no background, so that one cell
56	cannot take `ColorBackground`. `theme.StyleTextInput` sets every other state and
57	the cursor colour (`ColorHighlight`); the single-cell gap is accepted.
58	
59	**Drawing over an already rendered screen** (the command palette) goes through
60	`overlay.Compose` (`internal/ui/overlay`) and nothing else: it splices with
61	`x/ansi` and never cuts an escape sequence. `lipgloss.Place` stays for full-screen
62	modals. Never slice a styled line by bytes or runes.
63	
64	### Rule 117 : Centralized helpers of the `theme` package
65	
66	**Never recreate `bg()`, `padWithBg()`, `bgWrap()` locally.**
67	
68	| Function | Usage |
69	|----------|-------|
70	| `theme.Bg(s)` | Plain text with the app background |
71	| `theme.PadWithBg(content, width)` | Pad up to `width` with background |
72	| `theme.BgLine(s, width)` | Text + background + pad up to `width` |
73	| `theme.BgWrap(s, width)` | Background + pad on each line (multi-line) |
74	| `theme.EmptyLineBg(width)` | Blank line filled with background |
75	| `theme.OverlayBoxStyle()` | Standard style for overlay modals |
76	| `overlay.Compose(base, box, x, y, width)` | Box drawn over rendered lines, ANSI-safe |
77	
78	- **Inline text** → `theme.Bg("text")`
79	- **Full line** → `theme.BgLine("text", width)`
80	- **Multi-line paragraph** → `theme.BgWrap(text, width)`
81	- **Blank line** → `theme.EmptyLineBg(width)`
82	- **Modal overlay** → `theme.OverlayBoxStyle().Render(content)`
83	
84	### Rule 118 : Standardizing table and tab colors
85	
86	| Element | Foreground | Background |
87	|---------|-----------|------------|
88	| Table header | `ColorSecondary` | — |
89	| Selected row (normal) | **each column's own** | `ColorTableLineSelected`, bold |
90	| Selected row (error) | `ColorBlack` | `ColorError` |
91	| Active tab | `ColorBlack` | `ColorSecondary` |
92	| Inactive tab | `ColorDim` | `ColorCommandLineBg` |
93	
94	**Selected row (normal)** (§3.72 in the backlog; confirmed 2026-09-21). It used to
95	be one flat `ColorBlack` on `ColorSecondary`, dropping every column's own
96	colour — see Rule 122's "Selected row" section for why that used to be
97	mandatory and why it no longer is for this one variant: every cell now
98	repaints `ColorTableLineSelected` and bold **itself**, which is what makes
99	keeping the per-cell foreground safe instead of a return of the defect.
100	`error`, `busy` (`TableStylesForState`) and severity
101	(`TableStylesForSeverity`) are untouched — a solid background there still
102	means "this whole row is in that state," which per-cell colour would fight.
103	
104	`ColorTableLineSelected` (`table_line_selected` in a theme file) is its own
105	key rather than an alias of `ColorSeverityLow`, on purpose, so a theme tuning
106	"how muted is a LOW finding" no longer also retunes the selection highlight by
107	coincidence. Since DEVDESK-770 part B (D181) `ColorSeverityLow` is `ColorDim` on
108	the dark themes and the LOW badge text is `ColorBackground` on every level
109	(`TestSeverityBadgeTextIsTheAppBackgroundOnEveryTheme`): a badge is the
110	selected row of a finding, held to 4.5:1 (`TestEverySeverityBadgeReachesTextContrastOnEveryTheme`).
111	A theme that omits the two LOW keys gets `ColorDim` under `ColorBackground`.
112	
113	Mandatory centralized functions:
114	- `theme.DefaultTableStyles()` — base style
115	- `theme.TableStylesForState(state)` — `"normal"` or `"error"`
116	- `theme.TableStylesForSeverity(severity)` — `"CRITICAL"`, `"HIGH"`, `"MEDIUM"`, `"LOW"`, `"UNKNOWN"`
117	
118	Forbidden:
119	- ❌ Selection styles defined locally in views
120	- ❌ `ColorPrimary` for active tabs or headers (use `ColorSecondary`)
121	
122	### Rule 119 : No hardcoded hex color outside `colors.go`
123	
124	**A hex literal (`lipgloss.Color("#...")`, `color.RGBA{…}`) must appear ONLY in `internal/ui/theme/colors.go`.**
125	
126	One exemption: the body of `DefaultTheme` in `internal/ui/theme/manager.go`, the embedded default theme. `TestGuardNoHexColorOutsideColorsGo` (`internal/ui/theme/source_guard_test.go`) enforces both. The invalid-field underline colour is `theme.ColorInvalidField`, an alias (Rule 140).
127	
128	Palette variables are `color.Color` (`image/color`), not a Lip Gloss type. Read
129	one back with `theme.Hex(c)` (`#rrggbb`). A theme file is validated on load:
130	`theme.LoadTheme` refuses the whole file when a non-empty colour is not `#rgb`
131	or `#rrggbb` (see `docs/architecture/configuration.md`).
132	
133	3-level architecture:
134	
135	| Level | File | Role |
136	|--------|---------|------|
137	| **1. Base palette** | `colors.go` lines 6-32 | Raw hex colors (Catppuccin) |
138	| **2. Semantic colors** | `colors.go` lines 34+ | Aliases by usage, referencing the palette |
139	| **3. Styles** | `styles.go`, views | lipgloss styles using the semantic colors |
140	
141	If a hex color is needed with no semantic equivalent:
142	1. Add it to the base palette (`colors.go`, hex section)
143	2. Create a semantic alias that references the palette
144	
145	```go
146	// ✅ CORRECT
147	var ColorMaroon = lipgloss.Color("#eba0ac")  // in the base palette
148	ColorSeverityHigh = ColorMaroon              // in the semantic section
149	
150	// ❌ WRONG
151	ColorSeverityHigh = lipgloss.Color("#eba0ac")  // hardcoded hex in the semantic section
152	```
153	
154	`manager.go`'s fallbacks → reference `colors.go`, never hex values.
155	
156	### Rule 127 : Relative time — `theme.TimeAgo`
157	
158	**Every view displaying a relative time must use `theme.TimeAgo(t time.Time) string`** (`internal/ui/theme/timeago.go`).
159	
160	| Duration | Output |
161	|-------|--------|
162	| < 1 min | `"now"` |
163	| < 1 hour | `"59 min ago"` |
164	| < 24 h | `"23 hr ago"` |
165	| < 30 days | `"30 days ago"` |
166	| < 12 months | `"11 mo ago"` |
167	| else | `"99 yr ago"` |
168	| zero | `""` |
169	
170	Forbidden: local implementations, long formats, compact with no space.
171	
172	### Rule 129 : Interface and log language — English US only
173	
174	**All UI text and all logs must be in American English.**
175	
176	| Category | Rule |
177	|-----------|-------|
178	| Labels, titles, UI messages | ✅ English US |
179	| Error messages (footer) | ✅ English US |
180	| Help (`GetHelpContent`, `GetShortcuts`) | ✅ English US |
181	| Cell values, empty messages | ✅ English US |
182	| Logs (`log.Printf`) | ✅ English US |
183	| Code comments | ✅ English only (Rule 307) |
184	
185	```go
186	// ✅ CORRECT
187	m.footerStatus = "Loading workspaces..."
188	m.footerError = "Failed to refresh — check logs"
189	
190	// ❌ WRONG
191	m.footerStatus = "Chargement des workspaces..."
192	m.footerError = "Échec du rafraîchissement — voir les logs"
193	```

# entire-graph — instructions for coding agents (follow directly)

You have a deterministic local code graph: `entire graph` (functions, classes, methods,
types, routes + call/inheritance relations; no network). These instructions are FOR YOU, the
agent reading this file. Use the graph to narrow exploration without trading away correctness.

## The workflow (mandatory for locate/fix/change tasks)

Your FIRST action on any task that requires finding code must be ONE search:

    entire graph search --repo . --profile full --query "<the task or bug in one sentence>"

Then open the top hit's file with your file-read tool (pass a line range around the reported
line), inspect enough surrounding behavior to justify the change, and make the smallest complete
edit. Treat graph output as evidence, not an oracle.

1. SEARCH FIRST — never grep/find/cat to locate code before you have searched.
2. READ focused source around the result. Widen the check when aliases, generated code, dynamic

3. Use graph follow-ups only when they answer a real question. For impact or callers, prefer:

# CLAUDE.md

This file provides guidance to Claude Code (claude.ai/code) when working with code in this repository.

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **AI Collaboration Rule**:
> - **Planning**, **Brainstorming**, **Implementation** and **Bug fixes** are all
>   in scope. Planning is no longer delegated to Gemini (Antigravity).
> - Implementation plans go in `.claude/plans/` (see
>   [rules/planning.md](rules/planning.md)); design decisions that outlive a plan
>   are recorded in `docs/backlog.md`. Open work (stories, tasks, bugs) is tracked
>   in Plane, see the `## Plane` section of the root `CLAUDE.md`.
> - Always refer to [project-context.md](../project-context.md) for global project rules.
>   It sits in this repository, at the root. The absolute path this line used to
>   carry named a GitLab checkout that is no longer where DevDesk lives.

## Project Overview

DevDesk is a terminal-based TUI (Text User Interface) application built with Go and Bubble Tea framework. It provides DevSecOps functionality including:
- System status monitoring (HTTP/HTTPS, ICMP, DNS, SSL checks)
- GitLab integration (authentication, project explorer, multi-select clone)
- Security scanning (Trivy CVE/secret/license/misconfig + Gitleaks secrets)
- Container management with real-time metrics, on Docker or Podman (`app.container_engine`)
- OCI resource management (image scanning, container launching, network inspection)
- Network diagnostics (DNS, route, ICMP, TCP, TLS, HTTP; a Proxy row says whether a proxy variable applies, the checks themselves stay direct, DEVDESK-582) + real-time port monitoring (`K` stops a process: SIGTERM, up to 5 s, then a confirmed SIGKILL on Linux and macOS, at once on Windows; DevDesk itself, its direct parent, PID 1 and Windows PIDs 0 and 4 are refused; the identity is checked at each signal, DEVDESK-711) + this machine's interfaces + local port forwarding (unprivileged, loopback only) + a path trace under Diagnostics (Trace Path button, or `H` on the route row; no separate tab since DEVDESK-471) (native path trace, on native Linux, native Windows (IPv4 only, ICMP echoes through `iphlpapi`, DEVDESK-486) and WSL2: on macOS and WSL1 the button, `H`, `enter` and `ctrl+o` are greyed and the footer says why, DEVDESK-334; the column starts with this machine, its interface and its gateway; `ctrl+o` can start it from a running Docker Engine container instead (container and network rows, hops still traced from this machine); `H` on the Diagnostics route row opens the trace level on that host without starting it (greyed with the reason on an unsupported platform or a target the trace refuses; its interface and gateway rows reuse the Local route check's reading of the same address, read once, DEVDESK-473), and in the trace level `enter` starts or restarts it, `ctrl+o` picks the source, `esc` cancels then goes back where it came from; under WSL2 the source row says `WSL2 (VM), not the Windows host` with the networking mode, and in NAT mode the gateway and TTL 1 hop are tagged `Windows host (virtual switch)` only when proven, DEVDESK-333; the interface row says `no route` when the kernel proves there is none and `undetermined` when the routing table could not be read, a no-route error keeps the local rows, a trace that ends on the hop limit or the deadline folds its silent tail into one `silent` row and marks the `last to answer` hop, and the target refuses a `:port`, DEVDESK-335)
- Multi-context configuration management via YAML
- Local workspaces management with git metadata
- Claude Code session list (`:agent-usage` / `:au`): sessions found on this machine, by project and date, and per session the agent tree (orchestrator and sub-agents: types, models, tokens, share of the total; sortable by Total; also per agent a state (running / idle / done / unknown, idle after 5 min without a transcript line) shown as a status dot in the first column (the `running` dot blinks, DEVDESK-151) and as text, tool calls and duration; and an indicative cost per agent, `Est. cost` (orange from 75 % and red from 90 % of the session's estimated cost, when at least two agents are priced), from prices you write in the context YAML (`agent_usage.prices`, none shipped), with the session's `Billed` cost and `Unattributed` in the header, DEVDESK-47; a `Breakdown` colour bar per agent and, with `tab` inside a session, a Breakdown tab splitting the whole session's tokens by category, model and agent, as a percentage of tokens, DEVDESK-98). An open session updates live: read again every 2 s while active, only what was appended; paused after 5 min with no write and no unfinished sub-agent, when its transcript is gone, or while the terminal is not focused (header `Updates › paused`, then `paused (terminal not focused)`; `app.when_unfocused: run` keeps it live); `ctrl+r` reads it again in full. The sessions list itself is not live.

## Build and Development Commands

Tasks live in `mise.toml` — there is no Makefile. `mise tasks` lists them all.

```bash
# Development (fastest)
mise run dev          # Run directly with go run
go run .

# Build
mise run build        # Build binary to bin/dk
mise run run          # Build and run

# Testing
mise run test         # Run all tests
mise run cover        # Coverage per package
go test -v ./...      # Run all tests with verbose output
go test ./internal/command  # Run tests for specific package
mise run test-race    # Detect race conditions (critical for Bubble Tea Cmds)

# Code Quality
mise run fmt          # Format code
mise run vet          # Run go vet
mise run lint         # MANDATORY before commits - golangci-lint
mise run tidy         # Tidy dependencies
mise run check        # fmt + vet + lint + test in one go
mise run ci           # the five checks in order (fmt-check, vet, lint, build, test-race), stops at the first failure; unlike check it rewrites no file and also runs build and test-race. `test-race` is the only test run (`-race` covers `go test`); `mise run test` stays available alone for the fast local loop. CI runs fmt-check, vet, lint and build in the `Lint and build` job and `test-race` in the `Test` job, on every pull request, docs-only ones included (the docs-only shortcut applies to `Lint and build` only); the whole CI targets under 10 minutes, so run this locally before a PR to catch a red check early

# Installation
mise run install      # Install to $GOPATH/bin
```

`test-race` needs cgo and therefore a C compiler (`gcc`/`clang`) on `PATH`.

## Git, worktrees, pull requests — absolute rules

- Work happens in a worktree under `.worktrees/<branch>`, created from `origin/main`; the main checkout stays clean, on `main`.
- Never push directly to `main`: the Entire mirror rejects it, and so does the `main-protection` ruleset. Everything goes through a PR, merged once `Lint and build` and `Test` are green.
- Always use `gh -R anthnel/devdesk` (`origin` is `entire://`). There is one remote, `origin`; do not add a second one pointing at GitHub.
- A red `Entire Gates` check caused by Approvals alone does not block a merge (Findings, Checks, Up to date must stay green).
- In a sandbox, only commit; the host pushes, opens the PR and merges. Whoever creates a worktree removes it (never `git worktree prune` from the other side). The sandbox creates its own worktree; the host never creates one for it.
- Before creating a worktree or branch, pushing, opening/merging a PR or removing a worktree, load the `git-worktree-pr` skill.

## Releases

Only merging the release-please PR publishes a release; never merge it without the user's explicit agreement. After every merge on main, the orchestrating session loads the `release-flow` skill and checks the triggers.

## Architecture

The deep notes live in `docs/architecture/`, one file per area, and they are
**not** `@`-imported: an `@` would inline all of it into every session, which is
the thing this split exists to avoid. Read the file that covers what you are
touching, and update it in the same commit as the code.

| File | Covers |
|---|---|
| [`app-shell.md`](../docs/architecture/app-shell.md) | the router and its views, `ctrl+p` and the command parser, the keyboard vocabulary (`internal/ui/keymap`), greyed shortcuts, `shared.State`, cross-view messages, `netdiag.BackgroundMsg` (netdiag's own work, routed on or off screen), the jobs registry (`internal/jobs`), the one animation tick (blink phase, `app.motion`), the failure memory (`jobs.FailureKey`, `ChangedMsg.Failures`), the activity-column guard (`activity_guard_test.go`), the tab progress bar (OSC 9;4, `terminalProgress`), the window title (`windowTitle`, restored by `internal/termtitle`), the terminal hand-off to child processes (the exec wrapper `internal/ui/teaexec`, use it instead of `tea.ExecProcess`, D121) and the `:jobs` view |
| [`configuration.md`](../docs/architecture/configuration.md) | the config schema, the contexts, the migrations (`gitlab:` → `forge:`, `docker:` → `network:`), `agent_usage.prices`, and the configuration view |
| [`forge.md`](../docs/architecture/forge.md) | `internal/forge` and its two backends, `forge.Vocabulary`, the explorer's clone pipeline, and how the explorer reads the forge index (`internal/forgeindex`) and its `g` |
| [`workspaces.md`](../docs/architecture/workspaces.md) | the `ws` file icons (`internal/ui/fileicon`) and the sync (`F`) |
| [`filebrowser.md`](../docs/architecture/filebrowser.md) | `:files` (`internal/ui/filebrowser`, `internal/fsbrowse`), the path picker a form's path field opens with enter, and `theme.ShortPath` |
| [`viewer.md`](../docs/architecture/viewer.md) | `internal/viewer` + `internal/ui/viewer` — kinds, displays, colouring, search, follow |

### Credentials Management

No secret DevDesk holds is written to a file DevDesk owns. `internal/credentials`
implements the `Storage` interface three ways and `Select()` picks exactly one —
writing to several at once is what let the old "secure" option store a token in
the credential manager *and* in plaintext:

| Storage | Backend | Notes |
|---------|---------|-------|
| `KeyringStorage` | Windows Credential Manager / macOS Keychain / Secret Service | via `zalando/go-keyring`, no cgo. The default. |
| `GitCredentialStorage` | git's configured credential helper | Only when no configured helper is `store` (plaintext) or `cache` (memory with a timeout), by name, path or shell command: `approve` reaches every helper. Context-aware. |
| `MemoryStorage` | this process | Last resort, and deliberately worse: the auth view says nothing was saved. |

`Select(context, preference)` returns a `Selection{Storage, Backend, Detail}`.
The order is keyring → git credential → memory; `app.secret_backend` in the
context config pins the head of it (`auto`, `keyring`, `git-credential`). A
pinned backend that is unreachable falls through to memory rather than silently
to the other one. Every host store operation (the probe, `Save`, `Load`,
`Delete`) is bounded to 3 s: a store that does not answer, such as a locked
Secret Service waiting on an unlock prompt over SSH, is skipped like an absent
one, `Detail` says so, and it is not asked again while that call is stuck
(`internal/credentials/hoststore_bound.go`, DEVDESK-745).

The router resolves one `Selection` per context and keeps it in
`shared.State.Secrets`. It must be reused for the lifetime of the context — a
second `Select()` call yields a fresh `MemoryStorage` that cannot see what the
first one holds.

`MigrateLegacySecrets` runs at startup and on every context switch: a
`gitlab.token` or `registry.password` left in a context file by an older build
is moved into the store and deleted from the YAML, with the result reported in
the auth view. It takes the `Selection` and moves nothing when it does not
persist (memory), and removes a secret from the YAML only once it reads back
from the store; otherwise it stays and the note says so (DEVDESK-745).

## Testing

Test files follow Go conventions (`*_test.go`):
- `internal/command/parser_test.go` - Command parser tests
- `internal/app/app_test.go` - App router tests

Use table-driven tests where appropriate.

**`go test` does not detect races or explore fuzz targets.** `mise run test` runs
only the fuzz seeds, so `internal/agentusage` concurrency tests
(`TestConcurrent*`) need `mise run test-race`. To explore `FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull`
run `go test -fuzz=FuzzIncrementalMatchesFull -fuzztime=60s ./internal/agentusage`.

**HOME is shared across a test process.** `TestMain` in `internal/app` sets
`HOME` once for the whole process, so under `go test -count=N` a test finds
the files its own previous run wrote (context config, forge index cache), and
it fails from `-count=2` while `-count=1` passes (DEVDESK-36). A test that
writes under HOME isolates it with `t.Setenv("HOME", t.TempDir())` and
`USERPROFILE` too; in `internal/app`, call `isolateHome(t)` from
`harness_test.go` (already done by `routerAt`). `internal/ui/setup` is fixed
(DEVDESK-38): its `isolateHome(t)` helper in `model_test.go` is called by the
tests that write under HOME. Other packages whose TestMain does
`os.Setenv("HOME", …)` may have the same default. To find them:
`grep -rn 'os.Setenv("HOME"' --include=*_test.go`, then `go test -count=2` on each package.

**Never get a "free" port by `net.Listen("tcp", "127.0.0.1:0")`, reading the
port, then `Close()`, and letting the code under test bind it later.** Between
the close and the bind, any `bind(0)` can be handed that very port: an
`httptest.NewServer` in the same test, another test, another process on the
runner. The symptom is an intermittent `address already in use`, mostly in CI
(Linux gave the just-closed port back to about 1 `bind(0)` in 7,000; DEVDESK-35,
D85 in `docs/backlog.md`).

- If the code under test takes a port, call `loopback.ReservePort(t)`
  (`internal/testutil/loopback`). On Linux it holds a socket bound with
  `SO_REUSEADDR`, never listening, until `t.Cleanup`: `bind(0)` and `connect()`
  cannot take the port, but `net.Listen` can.
- Otherwise let the server bind `:0` and read the real port, or keep the
  listener open and hand it to the code under test.
- Off Linux, `ReservePort` keeps the old behavior and the window stays open
  (on Windows Go does not set `SO_REUSEADDR`). That is known, not a local bug.
- `internal/testutil/loopback` is imported from `_test.go` files only; nothing
  enforces it yet.

**Nexus tests replay recorded fixtures (DEVDESK-511, DEVDESK-580).** Three campaigns
in `internal/nexusfixture/fixtures/` (`catalog`, `cachedonly`, `access`) replay through
`fakenexus`: `mise run test` needs no bench, cluster or secret. A `record: pending` file is never
versioned (`TestNoPendingFixtureIsVersioned`); `DEVDESK_FIXTURE_RECORDING=1` only in a local recording session.
`nexus-bench record` without `--state` applies no state filter and can overwrite an `upstream-cut` fixture.
Bench writes go only through `nexus-bench:*` tasks and the guarded `DEVDESK_NEXUS_BENCH_SCENARIOS=1` test.
Dated measures live in `docs/measurements/`; a measure contradicting a criterion or the code is frozen and noted, never fixed in the same PR.

**Scanner containers and the proxy (DEVDESK-583, D164).** Every `run --rm` a scanner
issues goes through `containerRun{…}.cmd()` (`internal/scan/container_run.go`): the proxy
variables travel as `-e NAME` with the value in the child environment, never in argv. The
guard `TestContainerGuard*` (`internal/netproxy/container_guard_test.go`) fails on any other
`"run"` literal; only the two permanent exceptions in that file are allowed. The tests of
`internal/scan`, `internal/app` and `internal/ui/security` neutralise the seams
`proxyForward` / `containerForward` in their `TestMain`, so a developer's `HTTPS_PROXY` does not
change an exact argv. The `TestMain` of `internal/app`
also replaces `detectTools` (`internal/app/scan_tools.go`, production value `scan.Detect`) with an
empty report, so `App.Init` never runs the `trivy`, `gitleaks` and `plumber` of the machine
(DEVDESK-645); `TestInitDoesNotRunTheScannersOfTheHost` and `TestDetectToolsIsScanDetectInProduction`
guard it.
The renderers (helm, kustomize) run with the network cut (DEVDESK-767, D180):
`containerRun.Offline` (`--network none`, no proxy) from an image, `offlineEnviron` from a binary,
except kustomize with `scan.tools.kustomize.allow_remote_bases: true`; a refused remote base is the
K8S-RENDER finding `Overlay does not build: remote base blocked` (`remoteBlocked`).

**Tests and the host secret store (DEVDESK-610).** By default `credentials.Select` and
`KeyringAvailable` reach the real keyring of the machine (Secret Service over D-Bus on
Linux); a locked keyring blocks the whole suite until the timeout. A test binary that can
reach them isolates the store: `fakekeyring.Install()` in `TestMain`, then
`fakekeyring.Fresh(t)` (or `FreshUnreachable(t, err)` for a locked keyring) per test, from
`internal/testutil/fakekeyring`. `isolateHome(t)` already calls `Fresh` in `internal/app` and
`internal/ui/setup`. Two guards enforce it: at run time, any keyring or `git credential` call
in a test binary without the fake panics with `DEVDESK-610` and the operation; statically,
`TestHostStoreGuard*` (`internal/credentials/hoststore_guard_test.go`) fails on K1 (go-keyring
imported outside `internal/credentials`), K2 (`SwapHostStoreForTest` in non-test code) and K3
(`fakekeyring` imported by non-test code). The seam is `credentials.HostStore` and
`SwapHostStoreForTest`, reserved for tests (it panics outside a test binary). Limits: the
runtime guard only sees the paths a test runs; the static one misses an aliased package
name, a dynamic import and an external binary; `gitHelperUsable` reads the git config
unguarded; `Install` and `Fresh` are global, so no `t.Parallel`. See
`docs/architecture/configuration.md`, "Testing code that reaches the secret store".

**Tests and real signals (DEVDESK-708, DEVDESK-711).** A test must never signal a real process. In
`internal/ports` the only place that does is `realOS.kill(pid, want, sig)` (`internal/ports/procos.go`),
reached through the `procOS` seam, which also holds `identity` and `probe` (`Probe` reads the state, it
sends no signal). `selfPID`, `parentPID`, `goos` and `now` are seams too. A test substitutes them
(`useFakeOS(t, self, parent, goos)` in `seams_test.go`); in `internal/ui/netdiag` it replaces `processOps`
on the model, so `ports.Kill`, `ports.Terminate` and `ports.Probe` are never reached.
`IdentityForTest` and `DeferredIdentityForTest` panic outside a test binary.
Two guards enforce it: at run time, a real signal in a test binary panics with `DEVDESK-708`
unless the test called `allowRealSignals(t)`, which only a test that kills a child it
started itself may do (`TestKillEndsARealChildProcess`, `TestTerminateEndsARealChildProcess` in
`stop_real_test.go`); statically, `TestOnlyRealOSSendsASignal`
fails on a signalling call (`os.FindProcess`, `syscall.Kill`, `unix.Kill`,
`windows.TerminateProcess`, `.Kill(` or `.Signal(`) outside `(realOS) kill`. Limits: the static
guard misses an aliased import, another package and an external binary; the seams are global, so
no `t.Parallel`. See `docs/architecture/network.md`, "Seams and the signal guard".

**Test input and colour (DEVDESK-199).** Build keys only through
`internal/ui/testutil` (`Key`, `Keys`, `Type`, `Paste`, `Text`, `IsText`), never a
literal `tea.KeyPressMsg` or `tea.Key*`. `Key` returns a
`tea.KeyPressMsg` (`Keys` and `Type` return a message list), `Paste` a `tea.PasteMsg`; `Key` is strict: an unknown name
panics. The space key is built as a key (`Key("space")`), never matched through
`String()` (v1 `" "`, v2 `"space"`). Lip Gloss v2 has no global colour profile (`Style.Render` always emits full
colour), so a test needs no setup to check styling; it reads the SGR or strips it
with `ansi.Strip`. `internal/ui/testutil/source_guard_test.go` fails the suite on a
hand-built key, a `colorprofile` import outside `internal/app/profile_test.go` and
`internal/app/redraw_measure_test.go` or `SetColorProfile` in any `_test.go`. Paste tests
(`internal/app/paste_test.go`, `wrapped_input_test.go`, `component_form_test.go`):
a paste reaches the focused field, newlines become spaces in single-line fields,
and no key action fires (Rule 111).

**Space and key API (DEVDESK-200).** Production code matches the space key as
`keymap.Space`, never `" "`/`"space"`, and reads keys through `String()` only
(no `.Runes`, `.Alt`, `.Paste`, `tea.KeyType` or `tea.Key<Name>`). Update
handlers switch on `tea.KeyPressMsg`, never the `tea.KeyMsg` interface (it also
matches releases). A paste is a `tea.PasteMsg`, not a key (Rule 111). Guards in
`internal/ui/keymap` (`space_scan_test.go`, `legacy_key_scan_test.go`,
`viewport_keymap_scan_test.go`) fail the suite otherwise; limits are listed in
`docs/architecture/app-shell.md`.

## Critical Bubble Tea Rules

**NEVER modify model state inside a Cmd** (Rule 110) - Race condition:
- `Update()` is the ONLY place to modify model state
- `View()` is read-only
- `Cmd` functions do I/O and return messages

**NEVER use `style.Render()` inside `table.Row{}`** (Rule 122) - ANSI sequences corrupt all subsequent rows:

`Render() string` and `View() tea.View { return tea.NewView(m.Render()) }`; only the
router (`App.View()`) sets terminal state such as `AltScreen` and `BackgroundColor`. Components keep

## Critical rules (summary)

**Rule 110** — NEVER modify the model inside a `Cmd` → race condition. Only `Update()` modifies the model.

**Rule 122** — `Cell` returns plain text (it gets measured), color goes through `Style`. A `style.Render(...)` inside `Cell` gets truncated in the middle of its escape sequence and bleeds onto every following row.

**Rule 128** — A footer message goes through `components.FooterMessage`: three levels (neutral info, orange warning, red error), always centered, a single implementation. A table's loading state is shown in the footer, never in the body: with the shared activity dot (`Status.Activity`, `●`/`○`, `SetBlinkPhase`), for a view's own load as well as for work the router tracks. The braille spinner API is removed (DEVDESK-377): nothing under `internal/` imports `bubbles/v2/spinner` or names `Status.Spinner`, `SetSpinnerFrame`, `theme.SpinnerMessage` or `theme.SpinnerStyle` (`TestNoViewImportsTheBubblesSpinner`, `TestRemovedSpinnerSymbolsStayGone`), with no exception. A new `Activity` value not driven by the jobs registry must implement `WantsBlink()`, or the dot stays fixed.

**Rule 139** — A `datatable`'s body is always `m.table.View()`, never a loading screen or a message: an empty table (loading, nothing to list, a filter with no results) stays a table — a header, no rows. The count goes in `GetHeaderInfo`, the status in the footer.

**Rule 129** — All UI text and all logs in **English US**.

**Rule 140** — An invalid form field is underlined through `theme.StyleInvalidField` (the only entry point to the underline API), and the error is also in the footer at level Error, derived on every render. The underline is never the only carrier.

**Rule 133** — `bubbles/textarea` is forbidden. Use `components.WrappedInput` for any multi-line text field.

The per-topic TUI rule files above load when a matching file is read or edited; when reviewing a diff without opening files, read them explicitly.

because they were hard but because each altered something the user already saw,
so they needed a deliberate call rather than a drive-by fix. All five were then
decided together and fixed in one pass; see [§1.2](#12-the-five-parked-defects).

### 1.1 Fixed

**D181 — DEVDESK-770 part B: the severity badges reach 4.5:1 on the 13 themes, with their text set to the application background, and the gauge rail goes back to the frame border. Amends points 3 and 4 of D177. Decided (orchestrator, 2026-11-24, within the autonomy the user granted; the user can overrule).**

1. **Decided, HIGH.** `severity_high` is raised on five themes (latte `#e64553` to `#d61d2d`, one-dark `#be5046` to `#cf7d75`, solarized-dark `#cb4b16` to `#e8652e`, nord `#d08770` to `#d18a74`, solarized-light `#cb4b16` to `#c44815`), by the smallest lightness step (same hue and HSL saturation) that reaches 4.5:1 for the badge text on it. The other eight already held. CRITICAL and HIGH keep a CIE76 distance of at least 8 on every theme (`TestSeverityHighAndCriticalStayApart`); the closest pair stays macchiato at 8.9, latte moves from 11.7 to 9.0.
2. **Decided, LOW.** `severity_low` is `color_dim` on every dark theme (eight change, github-dark already was) and on the default theme (`#585b70` to `#979aad`). The LOW badge becomes a light badge with dark text, like HIGH, instead of a dark badge with light text that missed 4.5:1 on 10 of 13 themes (1.2 to 4.2). On the three light themes and github-dark `severity_low` already held and does not move.
3. **Decided, the badge text.** `severity_*_fg` of CRITICAL, HIGH, MEDIUM and LOW is `color_background` on every theme (`TestSeverityBadgeTextIsTheAppBackgroundOnEveryTheme`): a light badge carries dark text and a dark one light text, the foreground follows the theme's surface instead of a tone nobody holds to a ratio, and one number moves per badge. INFO and UNKNOWN keep their muted badge and are not decided here. The fallbacks of a theme that omits the LOW keys are `ColorDim` and `ColorBackground` (D177 had `ColorCmdLineBg` and `ColorText`, because `ColorDim` was then a light text tone under a light `ColorText`; both fallbacks now read on every theme since `ColorDim` is held to 4.5:1 on the background).
4. **Amends D177, point 3** ("the 13 shipped themes keep their own `severity_low`; the fallback is `ColorCmdLineBg`"): the shipped value is `color_dim` and the fallback is `ColorDim`. D177 point 2 (why `ColorSeverityLow` cannot follow `ColorDim` while the text on it stays light) is overtaken, not wrong: the text on it is no longer light. **Amends D177, point 4** ("the LOW badge foreground and the HIGH one stay under 4.5:1"): they reach it, `TestEverySeverityBadgeReachesTextContrastOnEveryTheme`.
5. **The gauge rail is the frame border again.** `GaugeTrackStyle()` is `ColorViewportBorder`, not `ColorSeverityLow` (§3.71 aliased it, then D177 kept the dark tone for it). With `ColorSeverityLow` at the tone of `ColorDim`, the track of every empty cell would be as bright as a label. The border is the tone the application already draws its lines in, and a rail is a line drawn inside the frame. **The cost, accepted and written here:** the border is held to 3:1 on the background (D179) but not on the selected row, where it is 2.2 to 2.8:1 on 11 of the 13 themes. The comparison with before (the rail, `ColorSeverityLow`, was 1.4 to 2.9:1 under the cursor on eight themes) covers only the themes that did not already reach 3:1; on four themes the rail gets worse: on the selected row it falls from 4.05 / 5.62 / 4.93 / 4.39:1 to 2.22 / 2.74 / 2.82 / 2.65:1 on latte / github-dark / github-light / solarized-light, from above 3:1 to below it (on the background, from 5.0 to 6.2:1 to 3.0, because the LOW tone was a text colour there). Under the cursor the rail is faint, and the number beside the gauge carries the value (the fill, the number and the glyph shape stay the carriers, Rule 122). A contrast ratio is not held for the rail, on purpose (`TestTheGaugeTrackIsTheViewportBorderOnEveryTheme` holds that it is the border, visible against the background and the selected row).
6. **Four token colours move.** The rail is now a tone `TestTokenColorsAreNotSeverityOrGaugeColours` (delta E 20 from the severity and gauge colours) keeps the token colours away from, and it caught four of them, which move by the smallest delta E, same hue, to the nearest tone that holds every other guard: latte `token_cache_read` `#607670` to `#5d746e` (delta E 1.0), github-light `token_cache_read` `#748db4` to `#6888bb` (7.3), nord `token_input` `#7b91bf` to `#7f9bd4` (7.0), solarized-light `token_cache_read` `#87836e` to `#878163` (5.3). The test is not loosened.
7. **A colour is never the only carrier of the level** (WCAG 1.4.1): the Severity cell spells the level out in full and never loses its column (`TestTheSeverityCellSpellsTheLevelOut`, `TestTheSeverityWordIsRenderedOnEveryRowAt80Columns`).
8. **Not decided here.** INFO and UNKNOWN, the `Yes` and success buttons, the error row (`ColorBlack` on `ColorError`, 3.05 on nord), and the severity counts of the inventory under the cursor, which stay at the 3:1 glyph threshold. Figures: `docs/measurements/2026-11-24-theme-text-contrast-3.md`.

**D178 — DEVDESK-769: a breadcrumb trail that is too long for its line drops its head and cuts its current segment, through `theme.RenderTrail`; the pills stay. Decided (architect and user, 2026-11-24; the user can overrule).**

1. **Defect.** The four breadcrumb rows (`ws`, the forge explorer, `:jobs`, the registry level of OCI resources) drew every pill with `PadWithBg(Bg(" ")+RenderTabs(...), width)`. Past the width the line overflowed, and the terminal wrapped it onto the next row.
2. **Decided.** The pills `" label "`, one cell apart, are kept. The current segment is always the last one. No "home" anchor is kept: when the trail does not fit, the head becomes one `…` pill and the largest tail that fits stays; if the current segment alone does not fit, it is cut at its end with `…`. Under 8 cells of room only the cut segment is drawn, under 3 nothing.
3. **Rejected.** Shrinking every label (no segment stays readable), keeping the first pill as an anchor (it costs cells the current segment needs), and a scrolling trail (a second navigation to learn on a row that is not navigable, Rule 123).
4. **Where.** `theme.FitTrail` and `theme.RenderTrail`; see `docs/architecture/ui-components.md`, "Breadcrumb trails that fit".

**D179 — DEVDESK-770 part A: the frame border reaches 3:1 on all 13 shipped themes, a departure from the third-party palettes. Decided (user, 2026-11-24).**

1. **Decided.** `ColorViewportBorder` reaches 3:1 (WCAG 1.4.11, a non-text object) against `ColorBackground` on every shipped theme (`TestEveryTextColourReachesItsContrastOnEveryTheme`). It lightens on the dark themes and darkens on the light ones; `color_border` follows `viewport_border` (the same hex on every theme). Ten themes move (github-dark `#30363d` to `#56616e` and github-light `#d0d7de` to `#8597a9` the most, delta E 18.7 and 25.1); default, mocha and macchiato already held.
2. **Why it departs from the palettes.** The shipped border tones were below 3:1 on ten themes (1.69:1 on nord, 2.30:1 on latte). The other colours of this part (`ColorSecondary`, `ColorPrimary` and their followers, the active tab, the inactive buttons) are retuned as in DEVDESK-764: same hue and saturation, the smallest lightness step; `cmd_line_inactive_fg` is aligned on `color_dim` instead. Figures: `docs/measurements/2026-11-24-theme-text-contrast-2.md`.
3. **Not decided here.** The LOW and HIGH badges and the gauge rail (part B), the non-chromatic signal of secondary text on solarized and latte (out of scope by decision of the user), the `Yes` and success buttons, INFO and UNKNOWN: "Not done here" of that note.

# Text contrast, part B of DEVDESK-770: the severity badges and the gauge rail

Measurement note of 2026-11-24. It follows `2026-11-24-theme-text-contrast.md` and `2026-11-24-theme-text-contrast-2.md`,
which are frozen: the second one lists the LOW and HIGH badges and the gauge rail under "Not done here", and this note
is what closes them. Nothing in those two notes is rewritten here. The decision is D181 in `docs/backlog.md`.

| | |
|---|---|
| Method | `theme.ContrastRatio(foreground, surface)` and `theme.ColorDistance` (CIE76 delta E), after `ApplyTheme(DefaultTheme())` then `ApplyTheme(<theme>)` for the default theme and each file of `themes/*.json`, read by a throwaway test (deleted) run on the commit before this change (themes read with `git show HEAD:themes/<name>.json`; for `default`, the old LOW pair `#585b70` / `#cdd6f4`) and on this one. The guards that hold the result are `TestEverySeverityBadgeReachesTextContrastOnEveryTheme`, `TestSeverityBadgeTextIsTheAppBackgroundOnEveryTheme`, `TestSeverityHighAndCriticalStayApart` (threshold 8), `TestEveryTextColourReachesItsContrastOnEveryTheme` (`ColorSeverityHigh` and `ColorSeverityLow`), `REDACTED` and `TestTheGaugeTrackIsTheViewportBorderOnEveryTheme` |
| Thresholds | 4.5:1 for the badge text on the badge, and for the badge colour on the background when it is painted as text (WCAG 1.4.3); 3:1 for the badge colour on the selected row (a glyph, Rule 118); CIE76 delta E of at least 8 between CRITICAL and HIGH. No ratio is held for the rail |
| Retuning rule | HIGH: same hue and same HSL saturation, lightness moved by steps of 0.005 away from the surfaces, by the smallest step (`minimalToneFor`, `tune_test.go`). LOW: `severity_low` is `color_dim` (already held to 4.5:1). The text of every badge is `color_background`. Tokens: same hue, lightness and saturation moved to the nearest colour (smallest delta E) that holds every guard of `tokencolors_test.go` |
| Themes | the 13 shipped ones. `default` and `catppuccin-mocha` are the same palette |

## What changed

| Key | Themes | Moves |
|---|---|---|
| `severity_high` | latte, one-dark, solarized-dark, nord, solarized-light | raised to 4.5:1 for the badge text |
| `severity_low` | the eight dark themes (frappe, macchiato, mocha, dark-plus, nord, one-dark, solarized-dark, tokyo-night) and `default` | set to `color_dim` (github-dark already was; the three light themes already held) |
| `severity_low_fg` | all 13 | set to `color_background` |
| `GaugeTrackStyle` | all 13 | `ColorSeverityLow` becomes `ColorViewportBorder` |
| `token_cache_read` / `token_input` | latte, github-light, solarized-light / nord | moved off the new rail tone |
| fallbacks in `ApplyTheme` | a theme that omits the LOW keys | `ColorCmdLineBg` and `ColorText` become `ColorDim` and `ColorBackground` |

Before this change, 5 of 13 themes had a HIGH badge under 4.5:1 (latte 3.48, one-dark 2.95, solarized-dark 3.26,
nord 4.39, solarized-light 4.27), and 10 of 13 a LOW badge under it (from 1.21 on solarized-light to 4.17 on
macchiato). After it, none of the four badges is under 4.5:1 on any theme; the lowest text-on-badge ratios are nord HIGH
and dark-plus LOW, both 4.52.
